## Overview

This Adyen documentation page describes PSD2 strong customer authentication options for an online payments integration that already implements 3D Secure. It separates three control layers: Adyen's default compliance handling, merchant-configured Dynamic 3D Secure rules, and per-transaction API preferences. This is provider compliance and request-routing guidance, not documentation for the independently versioned native 3DS2 SDK runtimes.

## Key takeaways

- Under the default option, Adyen's Authentication Engine determines whether to trigger 3D Secure and requests an exemption when applicable; the page says it does not trigger 3D Secure for out-of-scope transactions or when the issuer does not enforce it.
- Dynamic 3D Secure adds merchant-configured conditions, such as requesting authentication for transactions the merchant considers high risk. When no rule matches, the page routes handling back to the Authentication Engine.
- Per-transaction API preferences override Adyen's default PSD2 compliance-handling logic, including Adyen's check of whether the transaction is out of scope and its exemption selection and routing; relevant authentication fields also override Dynamic 3D Secure rules. Adyen recommends this route only for integrations with extensive PSD2 SCA and 3D Secure knowledge.
- An exemption request can be granted or denied by the issuer. In the documented authorization-only flow, a granted exemption must also be applied using authentication response values; a challenge preference does not determine whether the issuer challenges the shopper.

> [!warning] Scope and liability
> Applicability depends on regulations and scheme rules; this snapshot is not universal legal advice. The page also distinguishes chargeback liability based on who applies an exemption: liability stays with the merchant when a merchant, Adyen on its behalf, or its acquirer requests an accepted exemption, while issuer-applied exemptions shift liability to the issuer.

quotes.text: After you have implemented 3D Secure with Adyen, choose one of the [compliance options](#compliance-options) on this page to comply with PSD2 SCA.

* If you, Adyen on your behalf, or your acquirer requests an exemption and the request is accepted by the issuer, the liability stays with you.
* If the exemption is applied by the issuer, the liability shifts to the issuer.

Adyen offers the following methods for complying with PSD2 SCA:

* [Let Adyen handle PSD2 compliance by default.](#option-1-default-compliance)
* [Configure rules using Dynamic 3D Secure.](#option-2-dynamic-3ds)
* [Submit your preference for each transaction in your API request.](#option-3-specify-your-preference-in-the-api-request)

Our Authentication Engine will handle PSD2 SCA compliance for you. We will not trigger 3D Secure for out-of-scope transactions or if the issuing bank does not enforce 3D Secure. Our Authentication Engine will also handle requesting an exemption whenever applicable.

This option overrides our default PSD2 compliance handling logic, including checking if the transaction is out of scope, determining the most suitable exemption type, and evaluating whether to send the exemption in the authentication or authorization request. We recommend you use the API fields only if you have an extensive knowledge of PSD2 SCA regulations and the 3D Secure protocol.

## Adyen PSD2 SCA and 3D Secure

Adyen's online PSD2 SCA guidance assumes an online payments integration with 3D Secure and presents three provider-control layers: default handling by Adyen's Authentication Engine, merchant-configured Dynamic 3D Secure rules, and per-transaction API preferences. The API-preference route overrides Adyen's default PSD2 compliance-handling logic, including Adyen's check of whether the transaction is out of scope and its exemption selection and routing, so Adyen recommends it only for integrations with extensive PSD2 SCA and 3D Secure knowledge.

Applicability remains transaction-, regulation-, scheme- and issuer-dependent. Exemption requests can be granted or denied by the issuer, and challenge preferences do not control the issuer's challenge decision. Liability stays with the merchant when the merchant, Adyen on its behalf, or its acquirer requests an exemption and the issuer accepts it; liability shifts when the issuer applies the exemption. This provider compliance scope is distinct from [[adyen-3ds2-ios-sdk]] and [[adyen-3ds2-android-sdk]], which document native client transaction and challenge runtimes.
